name: Orbanism
summary: Orbanism is the governing approach of Viktor Orbán and Fidesz in Hungary since 2010. It rejects liberal democracy for an 'illiberal', Christian-national state in which the majority and the national community outrank individual rights and independent checks. It pairs strong sovereignty and anti-migration politics with pronatalist family policy, a work-based alternative to welfare, a flat tax, and an interventionist, nationalist economy.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Orbán insists on marriage between a man and a woman and the regime has doubled marriages through incentives (Enyedi), making the Christian family the basis of society; abolishing legal marriage is the opposite.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Orbán rejects multiculturalism and wants migrants kept out rather than integrated, but where admitted, adaptation is expected.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Orbanism offers a work-based alternative to welfare and values employment, so it favors keeping people in work.

basic-income.rationale: Orbán explicitly opposed universal basic income, favouring job-focused policy.

bound-labor.rationale: The work-based state compels work as a condition of aid but through municipal public work schemes, not legal bondage to a lord.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Enyedi: legitimacy stems from elections and top-down national consultations, other channels marginalised; ssoar: charismatic leadership and direct democracy.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Enyedi: ethnocentrism defines the community by lineage and patriotic attitudes, "not citizenship"; the citizenship law gave over a million diaspora Hungarians citizenship.

civilizational-union.rationale: Orbán: "we don't want to find ourselves in a United States of Europe, instead of integration"; Balázs Orbán wants a "Europe of nations" rather than a "European superstate".

clerical-rule.rationale: Orbán calls his state Christian but the leadership is political and secular; clerical supremacy is not part of it.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Balázs Orbán: authority comes "from the people"; Enyedi: paternalist populism treats elections as a crucial source of legitimisation.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Orbán: "Individual freedoms can never encroach on the interests of the community. There is indeed a majority that must be respected, that is the foundation of democracy"; National Interest: the mandate of the majority is the governing principle.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Orbán says Western liberal civilisation fails and Christian culture is superior.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: Böll: the work-based state involves "rejection of the idea of state benefits" and cuts to social services; Enyedi: benefits withdrawn from the unemployed and disabled.

decide-locally.rationale: Enyedi: paternalism stresses "the subordination of local and partial social institutions" to centrally endorsed guidelines; rights and resources moved from local to central government.

democracy-best.rationale: Orbán claims democracy but redefines it as majority-based and Christian, rejecting liberal democracy; "even when voters choose badly" is not a position he endorses.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Orbán holds that elections confer legitimacy and the majority's will outranks individual rights, though critics say the contests are not fair.

direct-votes.rationale: The regime uses referendums (migrant quotas, child protection) and top-down "national consultations" (Enyedi, National Interest); the ssoar paper lists direct democracy among its traits; elite-controlled channels remain.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Orbán declared Hungarians "not a mixed race" and said countries where Europeans and non-Europeans mingle "are no longer nations" (Outlook India); Enyedi: he values homogeneity. Stated of peoples, not as a law.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Enyedi: the regime projects a "hierarchical, male-centred nuclear family" and benefits redistribute workload by sex.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Enyedi: society is divided into deserving, hard-working and undeserving groups and resources rechannelled to the former; Böll: work-based state against the welfare state.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Orbán opposes mixing of peoples from different civilisations and ethnic diversity in Hungary, including the 2022 'mixed race' speech.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Orbán says individual freedoms can never encroach on the interests of the community.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Orbán explicitly seeks to give Hungarians (rather than foreign firms) ownership of key sectors such as banks, energy and retail, and the Fundamental Law and state policy reflect this economic nationalism.

elite-replacement.rationale: Enyedi: Orbán is "among the very few officeholders openly advocating the Great Replacement theory"; Outlook India: he hinted at the replacement theory.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Boell describes a 'permanent crisis' framing used to justify exceptional rule; adherents back extraordinary powers.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Orbán says the Commission "must not have a program", that direction belongs to national governments and wants a "Europe of nations" not a superstate; National Interest: Orbán resists any supranational orthodoxy overriding national law.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Boell and the Fundamental Law show majority-driven amendment and limits on constitutional courts, though a bill of rights exists.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Orbán rejects egalitarian economics and 'European socialism'.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Enyedi: the regime "considers ethnic homogeneity, and homogeneity in general, as major assets" and defines communities by lineage; Orbán: Hungarians are "not a mixed race".

flat-income-tax.rationale: Enyedi counts the flat tax among the regime's signature right-wing economic policies, kept despite being unpopular.

foreign-policy-non-interference.rationale: Foreign policy based on national interests rather than ideological crusades (Orbán at CPAC); Balázs Orbán: a sovereign foreign policy of openness, balance and pragmatism.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Enyedi: after 2010 domestic ownership rose by around 20% in banking, energy and media, and "marginalisation of foreign capital in specific economic sectors" is a regime aim.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Enyedi lists the ban on changing gender in official documents and the duty to protect "a self-identity corresponding to their sex at birth" among the regime's ideological policies; Orbán: "a person is either a man or a woman" (Outlook India).

gender-social-construct.rationale: Orbán: "a person is either a man or a woman"; the regime casts itself as a bastion against "gender propaganda" and what Enyedi calls "transgender operations" and "aggressive homosexual propaganda".

government-encourage-intercultural-conta.rationale: Orbán: liberal multiculturalism is rejected and Christian culture has priority; Enyedi: the regime values homogeneity.

government-nudges.rationale: Enyedi: paternalism "regards the state as the guardian and the educator of citizens".

harm-principle.rationale: The ideology limits individual freedom for community and Christian values.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Enyedi: school curricula and state exhibitions codify a nationalist-conservative historical memory.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Enyedi: lavish public spending on diaspora communities (€383 million in 2020), culture and churches abroad.

immigration-favours-shared-culture.rationale: Enyedi: "Cooperation between culturally similar nations is welcome... But those who represent different cultures must be kept out."

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The work-based state and Orbán's praise of work as the morally superior way to live tie reward to work, though neither text states a view on property income.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: The government nationalised private pension funds in 2010-11.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Orbán: "Individual freedoms can never encroach on the interests of the community"; Böll: collective national interests may override individual rights.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Orbán's 2014 speech holds Western liberal democracy failing and points to Singapore, China, Russia and Turkey as models for a Hungarian form.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Enyedi: Orbán advertises Hungary as a bastion against "the expansion of Islam"; Outlook India: he argues Christian and Muslim communities cannot coexist, while also saying the obstacle is "not Islam, but the bureaucrats in Brussels".

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Orbán: "a new era has begun, and this will be a right-wing era"; he frames politics as the right against progressives.

limit-population.rationale: Orbán calls demography the first and most important challenge, with far more funerals than baptisms, and wants a turnaround in births; he states no wish to limit population growth.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Split: Enyedi describes a "fundamentally right-wing economic policy" (flat tax, curtailed employee rights) alongside price caps, windfall taxes, public works and occasional nationalisation.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Orbán stresses culture, Christianity and national identity as the drivers of politics, rejecting historical materialism.

media-academia-power.rationale: Orbán: left-wing opinions "only appear to be in the majority when the media helps to amplify them"; the regime built parallel media and academic institutions to counter cultural hegemony.

military-force-for-human-rights.rationale: Orbán: "Progressives always think that foreign policy is a battle of ideologies... We need foreign policy based on our interests."

military-superiority.rationale: Orbán: the nation has "the political, economic, and soon enough, the physical means to defend" itself; "the most dangerous combination known in history is to be both rich and weak" (Enyedi).

minority-veto.rationale: Orbán says the majority is the foundation of democracy and individual freedoms cannot encroach on the community.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Enyedi: social care and education were handed to churches and para-public foundations with public financing.

morality-needs-religion.rationale: Orbán: liberal democracy was viable only while it kept its Christian roots; "democracy could not exist without Christianity".

more-religion-public.rationale: Orbán calls Hungary a Christian state and says democracy could not exist without Christianity, though the stress is cultural-civilisational rather than devotional.

multipolar-world.rationale: Orbán champions national sovereignty against Brussels and a multipolar order, as his speeches state.

nation-first.rationale: Balázs Orbán: Orbánism is "sovereign and patriotic politics" and "we are neither pro-Russian nor pro-Ukrainian, we are pro-Hungarian"; Orbán: "We need foreign policy based on our interests."

national-church-status.rationale: Enyedi: the alliance with the historical churches dates to 1996 and the church law created a hierarchy among churches, privileging them.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Orbán insists the Fundamental Law and national interest outrank EU and international bodies in matters of sovereignty.

national-mission.rationale: Orbán: "Progressives always think that foreign policy is a battle of ideologies... We need foreign policy based on our interests."

national-rebirth.rationale: Orbán's "national transition" turns against the liberal zeitgeist; the West is in decay (Böll), and the regime builds a new national system.

national-self-determination.rationale: Orbán calls the Atlantic Charter, which promotes "self-determination and self-governance of nations", an illiberal document he endorses.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Orbán rejects welfare and basic-income schemes in favour of a work-based state.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Enyedi: a paternalist, redistributive state running social transformation programmes, price caps and public works; Böll: the state organises the nation as a community.

one-party-rule.rationale: Elections are treated as a crucial source of legitimacy (Enyedi), though Orbán wanted a "central political field of force" party (Böll); no exclusive right claimed.

open-borders.rationale: Orbán calls migration an outside threat Hungary has defended itself against and ordered the 2015 border barrier, so open borders contradict the programme.

party-controls-media.rationale: Enyedi: the message is spread through media owned or sponsored by the state; Orbán: "we must have our own media".

patriotic-education.rationale: Enyedi: the nationalist-conservative curriculum is imposed on all public schools and the regime expects education to defend traditionalist values.

person-over-state.rationale: Orbán says individual freedoms can never encroach on the interests of the majority and that the national community outranks individual rights.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: The movement is populist and presents Brussels and liberal elites as corrupt, though its own record is criticised.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Orbán wants to reduce the Commission's role and keep national governments in charge, opposing more pooling.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Illiberal conservatism and the "national transition" centre on keeping national culture (Enyedi quoting Fodor: illiberals "protect their homeland, preserve national culture"); Balázs Orbán: the nation is the frame for the challenges of our time.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Enyedi: paternalist populism includes "caps on a wide range of prices (especially utilities and food)".

price-controls-fight-inflation.rationale: Enyedi: paternalist populism includes "caps on a wide range of prices (especially utilities and food)".

promote-democracy-abroad.rationale: Orbán: "Progressives always think that foreign policy is a battle of ideologies... We need foreign policy based on our interests."

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Orbán: "instead of migrants, money should be given to European families so they can have more children"; Enyedi: giving birth can exempt mothers from income tax and student-loan repayment.

proportional-representation.rationale: Boell describes electoral changes favouring governing parties; adherents prefer majoritarian outcomes that give clear mandates.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Enyedi: support for Hungarian-speakers in neighbouring countries has been present since the party's start; the Bethlen Foundation spent 12 times more in 2020 than in 2011.

race-based-immigration-restrictions.rationale: Orbán contrasts Europeans mixing among themselves with a 'mixed-race world' of Europeans and non-European arrivals and calls for stopping the latter; Enyedi describes the defence of white Christian culture against migration.

race-social-construct.rationale: Orbán speaks of "mixed race" and racial homogeneity as real and essential to the nation.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Orbán says democracy cannot exist without Christianity and calls the state Christian, so faith and tradition are not subordinated to reason alone.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Orbán built a border fence in 2015, rejects EU quotas and calls migration an existential threat.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Orbán says the nation defended itself against "the attacks of Brussels, the IMF, and the migrants".

religion-illusion.rationale: Orbanism defines Hungary as a Christian-national state and treats Christian culture as lasting, so it rejects the view that religion will fade.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Enyedi: Fidesz demanded the state differentiate between churches and support only those that "do not contradict our values on the issues of family and nation"; the church law created a hierarchy among churches.

religious-nation.rationale: Enyedi: civilisation to be defended is white Christian culture; Orbán predicted border guards would stop non-Christian EU citizens; but belonging is also defined by lineage and patriotism.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Orbanism treats foreign-financed civil society as political interference, and Hungary created a Sovereignty Protection Authority in 2024 to investigate foreign influence.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: In 2014 Orbán held up Singapore, China and Russia as models and the work-based state subordinates liberal freedoms to competitiveness.

results-over-ideology.rationale: Enyedi: Fidesz "identifies as a pragmatic political force that is driven by pure common sense"; Balázs Orbán stresses pragmatism.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: Orbán wants EU money directed to families rather than migration, a nationalist priority over global aid.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Orbán: "we insist that marriage in Hungary is between a man and a woman" (National Interest); Enyedi: the 2011 constitution "doesn't only exclude the possibility of same-sex marriage" and the regime rests on the Christian family model.

separate-church-state.rationale: Orbán: the state cannot stay neutral on culture and family and Hungary is "the illiberal, Christian state"; Enyedi: this conservatism is hostile to state neutrality and allies with the churches.

separated-powers.rationale: Enyedi: illiberal conservatism is "hostile to checks and balances"; but she also notes the 2011 constitution contains counter-majoritarian bodies, so a mixed record.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Orbán: "a person is either a man or a woman"; the regime casts itself as a bastion against "gender propaganda" and what Enyedi calls "transgender operations" and "aggressive homosexual propaganda".

shared-human-nature.rationale: Orban defends a Christian view of the person and family against what he calls gender ideology, implying a fixed human nature.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Enyedi describes its illiberal conservatism as projecting the hierarchical, male-centred nuclear family as the unit of political society.

single-common-good.rationale: The government alone defines the national interest, and says individual interests yield to the community.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Orbanism took over and reshaped existing state institutions through the 2011 Fundamental Law rather than dismantling the state.

state-as-business.rationale: Orbanism sees the state as a national and moral community, not a business; though 'competitiveness' language appears in 2014.

state-directs-investment.rationale: The government uses public funds to build a national middle class and champion firms.

state-harmful.rationale: Enyedi: paternalism "regards the state as the guardian and the educator of citizens"; the ssoar paper lists etatism among Orbánism's characteristics.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Orbán's state is explicitly Christian ("Christian liberties", democracy cannot exist without Christianity).

state-supports-good-ways-of-life.rationale: Orbán: the state cannot remain neutral on culture, family and "what sort of people are in your own country"; Enyedi: public support is conditional on compliance with official cultural norms.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Split within one statement: Hungary "will not automatically join a bloc" but "it is not about neutrality" (Balázs Orbán).

strong-leader.rationale: Orbán's project concentrates power in the government to avoid gridlock and defends it as serving the national will, which is central to the model.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: The regime's economic policy is "fundamentally right-wing" with a flat tax; resources are redirected toward the hard-working and deserving, not by taxing the wealthy more (Enyedi).

total-state.rationale: The state is dominant but not total in the fascist sense; the economy retains private enterprise.

traditional-family.rationale: Enyedi: illiberal conservatism "promotes traditional family structures, social order, and religious (Christian) legacies" and "projects the hierarchical, male-centred nuclear family as the unit of the political society"; Balázs Orbán: "We believe in traditional values such as the family, the nation and order".

turn-back-illegal-migrants.rationale: Orbán: "We will not give up the right to defend our borders, to stop migrants"; Enyedi: a fence and rejection of virtually all asylum seekers.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Böll: the work-based state satisfies "welfare-chauvinism" among right-wing voters; Enyedi: benefits go to married, employed native couples and are withdrawn from the unemployed.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Orbán says a national system values service to the nation and participation over private choices.

work-centre-of-life.rationale: Orbán's project is the "work-based state" and "work-based society" (Böll); Orbán calls "work, studying, healthy lives, paying taxes" morally superior (Index).

work-for-welfare.rationale: The work-based state is the defining social policy; Boell describes the public work scheme as central to the 'work-based' alternative to welfare.

keyFigures.role: Fidesz leader and Hungarian prime minister whose governance gave the ideology its name

evidence.quote: Orbánism is benefiting in the same time from the Putin example and from Hungarian traditions and philosophical history.
Viktor Orbán’s philosophy and ideology, called Orbánism, is built on Nationalist, often Xenophobic rhetoric and policies.

scope: Orbanism is the ideology and governing method of Viktor Orbán and Fidesz in Hungary, above all since 2010: the self-declared 'illiberal state' (Orbán's 2014 Băile Tuşnad speech), in which the nation and its governing party outrank individual rights and independent checks (Böll Foundation, s4), with Christian-national, family-centred social conservatism, anti-migration sovereignty politics, a majoritarian view of democracy, a 'work-based' economy, and conflict with EU institutions (National Interest, s6; Outlook India, s8). Scholars describe it as an ideology of illiberal conservatism, civilisationalist ethnocentrism and paternalist populism (Enyedi, s7); others see mainly a vehicle for power. It covers the Orbán regime's own programme and its imitation by allies; it excludes Hungarian conservatism and Fidesz's pre-2010 liberal phase, Horthyism, and the wider family of 'illiberal democracy' elsewhere, except as the sources tie them to Orbán.
